subject: Biology
summary: Covers applied medical, agricultural, environmental, and industrial biotechnology: Agricultural applications (Green Revolution limits, GMO advantages, Golden Rice provitamin A beta-carotene with daffodil psy and Erwinia crtI genes); Insect resistance in Bt crops (Bacillus thuringiensis crystalline protoxin, midgut alkaline pH solubilization, midgut protease activation, epithelial pore lysis, gene specificity: cry1Ac/cry2Ab for cotton bollworms, cry1Ab for corn borer); Pest resistance via RNA Interference (RNAi in transgenic tobacco against Meloidogyne incognita root-knot nematode via host dsRNA, Dicer 21-23 bp siRNA, and RISC mRNA degradation); Plant tissue culture (Cellular totipotency, MS medium, micropropagation producing somaclones, virus-free meristem culture, somatic hybridization using cellulase/pectinase protoplasts and PEG to generate Pomato); Medical biotechnology (Recombinant human insulin Humulin by Eli Lilly 1983: Chain A 21 AA and Chain B 30 AA expressed separately in E. coli and joined in-vitro by 2 disulfide bonds, mature insulin lacks C-peptide 31 AA); Gene therapy (1990 ADA deficiency SCID protocol in 4-year-old using retroviral vector in cultured T-cells requiring periodic re-infusions, permanent embryonic bone marrow cure); Molecular diagnostics (PCR, ELISA, 32P-labeled single-stranded probes where mutated genes fail to appear on X-ray film); Stem cell technology (ESCs from blastocyst ICM, Yamanaka iPSCs using Oct4/Sox2/Klf4/c-Myc); Transgenic animals (>95% mice, Rosie cow 1997 with 2.4 g/L human alpha-lactalbumin milk, alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema, disease models, polio vaccine safety); and Biosafety/Ethics (GEAC statutory mandate under MoEFCC, Biopiracy patent revocations: Basmati rice RiceTec, Turmeric, Neem).

sections.title: Agricultural Biotechnology: GMOs & Golden Rice
sections.topic: Green Revolution Limitations, GM Crop Advantages, & Provitamin A Biofortification

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: GM crops overcome Green Revolution chemical limits, providing abiotic resilience, pest resistance, and nutritional biofortification (Golden Rice enriched with Provitamin A beta-carotene).

sections.codeSnippet:
ADVANTAGES OF GM CROPS
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┴──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
ABIOTIC RESISTANCE   PEST RESISTANCE              NUTRITIONAL ENRICHMENT EFFICIENT MINERAL USE
├── Cold & Salt      ├── Bt Cotton (Bollworms)    └── Golden Rice        └── Prevents early soil
└── Drought & Heat   └── Bt Corn (Corn Borer)         (β-Carotene)           nutrient exhaustion
sections.content:
### 1.1 GMOs & Golden Rice
- **GM Crops**: Enhance abiotic stress resistance, pest tolerance, and nutrition.
- **Golden Rice**: Biofortified with **$\beta$-Carotene (Provitamin A)** using daffodil (*psy*) and *Erwinia* (*crtI*) genes to fight blindness.

sections.title: Bt Crops: Cry Toxin Activation & Gene Specificity
sections.topic: Bacillus thuringiensis, Inactive Cry Protoxins, Alkaline Midgut Solubilization, & cry1Ac/cry2Ab/cry1Ab

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Bt Cry protoxins are solubilized by alkaline pH (>8.5) in insect midguts and cleaved into active pore-forming toxins. cry1Ac & cry2Ab control cotton bollworms; cry1Ab controls corn borer.

sections.codeSnippet:
Bt CRY TOXIN MIDGUT SOLUBILIZATION CASCADE
                   
   Inert Insecticidal Cry Protoxin Crystals synthesized in Bacillus thuringiensis
                                          │
   Ingested by Target Insect Larva ───────┘
               │
   Reaches Insect Midgut ──► ALKALINE pH solubilizes crystalline protoxin
                                          │
   Midgut Proteases cleave protoxin ──────┴──► ACTIVE CRY TOXIN
                                                    │
   Binds Cadherin Receptors on Midgut Epithelial Cells ──► Forms Pores & Causes Lysis
                                                    │
   Insect Gut Swells, Lyses, and Insect Dies of Septicemia
sections.content:
### 2.1 Bt Cry Toxins
- **Activation**: Inactive crystal protoxin $\rightarrow$ solubilized in **alkaline midgut $\text{pH}$** $\rightarrow$ proteolytically cleaved $\rightarrow$ creates lytic epithelial pores.
- **Specificity**: `cry1Ac` & `cry2Ab` (Cotton bollworm); `cry1Ab` (Corn borer).

sections.title: Pest Resistance via RNA Interference (RNAi)
sections.topic: Meloidogyne incognita, Transgenic Tobacco, Sense & Anti-Sense RNA, Dicer, & RISC Complex

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: RNAi silences Meloidogyne incognita root-knot nematode in tobacco. Ingested host dsRNA is diced into 21-23 bp siRNAs, guiding RISC to degrade complementary nematode mRNA.

sections.codeSnippet:
RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAi) CASCADE
                        
   Agrobacterium vector inserts nematode-specific genes into Tobacco Genome
                                          │
   Plant transcribes BOTH Sense and Anti-sense RNA
                                          │
   Base-pairing forms Double-Stranded RNA (dsRNA) inside plant cells
                                          │
   Nematode feeds on transgenic tobacco root tissue ──► Ingests plant dsRNA
                                          │
   Endogenous Dicer Enzyme cleaves dsRNA into 21–23 bp siRNA (Small Interfering RNA)
                                          │
   siRNA incorporates into RISC (RNA-Induced Silencing Complex)
                                          │
   RISC uses single-stranded siRNA to target & DEGRADE complementary Nematode mRNA
                                          │
   Specific Nematode Gene Silenced ──► Nematode cannot survive in transgenic host!
sections.content:
### 3.1 RNAi Mechanism
- **Host dsRNA**: Transcribes sense and antisense strands $\rightarrow$ forms **dsRNA**.
- **Silencing**: Nematode ingests dsRNA $\rightarrow$ **Dicer** cuts into siRNA $\rightarrow$ **RISC** degrades nematode mRNA.

sections.title: Plant Tissue Culture: Totipotency & Micropropagation
sections.topic: Gottlieb Haberlandt, Cellular Totipotency, Explant, MS Medium, & Somaclones

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Totipotency allows single plant cells/explants to regenerate into whole plants on MS medium (sucrose, inorganic salts, auxin/cytokinin). Micropropagation clones thousands of somaclones.

sections.codeSnippet:
TISSUE CULTURE PRINCIPLES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   CELLULAR TOTIPOTENCY                                      MICROPROPAGATION
   The innate capacity of a single plant cell/explant to      Rapid in-vitro multiplication yielding
   regenerate into a whole intact plant (Gottlieb Haberlandt). thousands of genetically identical Somaclones.
sections.content:
### 4.1 Tissue Culture
- **Totipotency**: Whole plant regeneration from explants (*Haberlandt*).
- **Nutrients**: MS medium + Auxin/Cytokinin $\rightarrow$ Callus $\rightarrow$ **Somaclones**.

sections.title: Meristem Culture & Somatic Hybridization (Pomato)
sections.topic: Virus-Free Plants, Protoplast Isolation, Cellulase/Pectinase, PEG Fusion, & Cybrids

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Meristem culture generates virus-free plants. Somatic hybridization strips cell walls using cellulase and pectinase, fusing naked protoplasts with PEG to create Pomato.

sections.codeSnippet:
SOMATIC HYBRIDIZATION WORKFLOW
                        
   Parent Plant A (Potato) ──► Enzymatic Wall Digestion (Cellulase + Pectinase) ──► Naked Protoplast A
   Parent Plant B (Tomato) ──► Enzymatic Wall Digestion (Cellulase + Pectinase) ──► Naked Protoplast B
                                                    │
                               Protoplast Fusion induced by PEG (Polyethylene Glycol)
                                                    │
                               Regenerates Cell Wall ──► Callus ──► SOMATIC HYBRID (Pomato)
sections.content:
### 5.1 Meristems & Protoplasts
- **Virus-Free Plants**: Apical meristems divide faster than viruses.
- **Somatic Hybrids**: Cellulase/Pectinase strip cell walls $\rightarrow$ **PEG** fuses protoplasts (*Pomato*).

sections.title: Recombinant Human Insulin (Humulin & Eli Lilly)
sections.topic: Pro-Insulin vs Mature Insulin, C-Peptide Cleavage, Disulfide Bonds, & E. coli Recombinant Production

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pro-insulin contains C-peptide (31 AA). Mature insulin lacks C-peptide and has Chain A (21 AA) & Chain B (30 AA) linked by 2 disulfide bonds. Eli Lilly synthesized chains A & B separately in E. coli and combined them in-vitro.

sections.codeSnippet:
PRO-INSULIN vs MATURE INSULIN
                        
   PRO-INSULIN (Inactive):   A-Chain (21 AA) ── [ C-PEPTIDE (31 AA) ] ── B-Chain (30 AA)
                                                     │
   MATURE INSULIN (Active):  A-Chain (21 AA) ═════════════════════════════ B-Chain (30 AA)
                             (Linked by 2 Inter-chain Disulfide Bonds)
sections.content:
### 6.1 Recombinant Insulin
- **Structure**: Chain A ($21\text{ AA}$) + Chain B ($30\text{ AA}$) held by $2\text{ disulfide bonds}$; **Mature insulin LACKS C-peptide**.
- **Eli Lilly (1983)**: Expressed Chain A & B separately in *E. coli*, joined via disulfide bonds.

sections.title: Gene Therapy: ADA Deficiency & SCID Protocol
sections.topic: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency, 1990 Clinical Trial, Retroviral cDNA Delivery, & Permanent Embryonic Cure

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: ADA deficiency causes SCID. The 1990 gene therapy used retroviral vectors to introduce ADA cDNA into cultured T-lymphocytes (requiring periodic re-infusions). Permanent cure requires embryonic bone marrow gene insertion.

sections.codeSnippet:
ADA DEFICIENCY & SCID PATHOLOGY
                      
   Mutation in ADA Gene on Chromosome 20 ──► Loss of Adenosine Deaminase enzyme
                                                                │
   Accumulation of toxic dATP inside Lymphocytes ◄──────────────┘
                                │
   Destruction of T- and B-Lymphocytes ──► Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID)

                        CLINICAL GENE THERAPY PROTOCOL (1990)
                        
   Harvest Lymphocytes from blood of 4-year-old SCID female patient
                                          │
   Culture Lymphocytes in-vitro
                                          │
   Introduce functional human ADA cDNA using a Disarmed Retroviral Vector
                                          │
   Re-infuse genetically engineered lymphocytes back into the patient
                                          │
   LIMITATION: Patient requires periodic re-infusions because lymphocytes are not immortal!
sections.content:
### 7.1 Gene Therapy & SCID
- **ADA Deficiency**: Toxic dATP destroys lymphocytes $\rightarrow$ SCID.
- **1990 Trial**: Retroviral *ADA* cDNA in T-cells (requires periodic re-infusions; permanent cure requires embryonic stem cells).

sections.title: Molecular Diagnostics: PCR, ELISA, & Nucleic Probes
sections.topic: Early Sub-Clinical Diagnosis, PCR Pathogen Detection, ELISA Principle, & Radioactive 32P Probes

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Molecular diagnostics detects sub-clinical disease: PCR (amplifies low viral DNA), ELISA (antigen-antibody binding), and 32P radioactive probes (mutated genes fail to hybridize and do not appear on X-ray film).

sections.codeSnippet:
MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION (PCR)     ELISA ASSAY                 RADIOACTIVE NUCLEIC PROBES
├── Amplifies ultra-low pathogen    ├── Antigen-Antibody        ├── Single-stranded ³²P-DNA/RNA
│   DNA/RNA sequences               │   interaction test        │   probe hybridizes to DNA matrix
└── Detects HIV in early asymptomatic├── Uses enzyme conjugate  └── Mutated genes DO NOT appear
    patients & p53 mutations          (Peroxidase)                  on X-ray film (no match)
sections.content:
### 8.1 Molecular Diagnostics
- **PCR**: Detects early HIV and oncogene mutations.
- **ELISA**: Antigen-antibody interaction.
- **Autoradiography Probes**: Mutated genes **do not appear** on X-ray film.

sections.title: Stem Cell Technology: ESCs & Yamanaka iPSCs
sections.topic: Potency Spectrum (Totipotent, Pluripotent, Multipotent), Blastocyst ICM, & Yamanaka Factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Stem cells span totipotent, pluripotent (ESCs from blastocyst ICM), and multipotent. Shinya Yamanaka (Nobel 2012) created iPSCs from adult somatic cells using Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc.

sections.codeSnippet:
STEM CELL POTENCY SPECTRUM
                               │
     ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
     ▼                         ▼                         ▼
  TOTIPOTENT               PLURIPOTENT               MULTIPOTENT
  ├── Zygote & early       ├── Embryonic Stem Cells  └── Adult Stem Cells
  │   blastomeres          │   (ESCs from ICM)           (Hematopoietic stem
  └── Can form whole       ├── iPSCs (Yamanaka)          cells in bone marrow)
      fetus + placenta     └── Forms all 3 germ layers
sections.content:
### 9.1 Stem Cells & iPSCs
- **ESCs**: Pluripotent cells from Inner Cell Mass (ICM) of blastocysts.
- **iPSCs**: Reprogrammed adult somatic cells using **Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc** (*Yamanaka*).

sections.title: Transgenic Animals: Rosie Cow, Emphysema, & Disease Models
sections.topic: Transgenic Mice Models, Rosie the Cow (alpha-Lactalbumin), alpha-1-Antitrypsin, Vaccine Safety, & Toxicity Testing

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Transgenic animals (>95% mice) model diseases, test polio vaccines, and produce human proteins: Rosie cow (2.4 g/L alpha-lactalbumin) and alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema.

sections.codeSnippet:

     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
PHYSIOLOGICAL STUDIES   DISEASE MODELS              BIOLOGICAL PRODUCTS  VACCINE SAFETY
Investigating gene      Animal models for Human     ├── Rosie Cow        ├── Testing Polio
regulation & growth     diseases (Cancer,           │   (α-lactalbumin)      vaccine safety
factors (IGF-1).        Alzheimer's, Cystic Fib.)   └── α₁-Antitrypsin       on transgenic
                                                        (Treats Emphysema)   mice first
sections.content:
### 10.1 Transgenic Animals
- **Mice ($>95\%$)**: Disease models and polio vaccine safety testing.
- **Rosie Cow (1997)**: Milk contains $2.4\text{ g/L}$ human **$\alpha$-Lactalbumin**.
- **$\alpha_1$-Antitrypsin**: Produced in transgenic sheep milk to treat **Emphysema**.

sections.title: Biosafety, GEAC, Biopiracy, & High-Yield Traps
sections.topic: GEAC Mandate, Biopiracy Cases (Basmati Rice, Turmeric, Neem), & Master Glossary

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: GEAC is an Indian statutory committee regulating GM safety. Biopiracy patent disputes on Basmati rice (RiceTec), Turmeric, and Neem were successfully revoked by India.

sections.content:
### 11.1 Biosafety, GEAC & Biopiracy
- **GEAC**: Indian statutory committee under MoEFCC.
- **Biopiracy**: Revoked patents on Basmati rice (*RiceTec*), Turmeric, and Neem.
